subject.title: Feature: fallbackChannel for hook mappings when primary delivery fails

question: Should hook mappings support automatic cross-channel delivery fallback, and if so, which failures may retry and how must each fallback recipient, account, and privacy boundary be declared?
rationale: The missing feature is not a mechanical field addition: automatic delivery to another channel can duplicate messages or expose content to a different audience, and existing single-target and outbound-selection behavior does not answer those policy questions.

options.title: Adopt explicit ordered targets
options.body: Add an opt-in ordered target list whose every channel, recipient, and account is declared, and retry only definite pre-acceptance failures.

options.title: Keep one delivery target
options.body: Retain current single-target hooks and document a user-managed reliability pattern instead of automatic cross-channel delivery.

options.title: Design a narrower recovery path
options.body: Add a hook failure event or inbox notification surface first, then defer cross-channel resend until recipient and duplicate semantics are settled.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit ordered targets
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in ordered target list whose every channel, recipient, and account is declared, and retry only definite pre-acceptance failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and adjacent gateway configuration history provide the strongest available signal for the hook-delivery policy boundary.
